A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RiTTA and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the substantial revision and relocation of content.

before.justification: v1 reports original TTA benchmarking, Tango finetuning results, and PANNS detector experiments, including the appendix comparison of detector mAP before and after finetuning.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and adds TangoFlux benchmarking, GPT-4 agentic comparisons, gated prompt tuning experiments, and component ablations.

M1.justification: v1 Section 4 proposes finetuning Tango's diffusion model while fixing the other components. v4 Section 5 introduces relation and event prompts, text-conditioned cross-attention, sparse entmax gating, and auxiliary classification losses. These prompts are jointly trained with Tango's UNet or TangoFlux's Transformer blocks, constituting a substantive new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same constructed benchmark covering four relation categories, 11 sub-relations, and 25 audio event classes, with seed audio from Freesound and VCTK. The PANNS training and testing coverage is also retained. New model and agentic comparisons use this existing coverage; open-ended generation is only proposed as future work.

E2.justification: v4 Table 4 retains the original seven model configurations and adds TangoFlux plus GPT-4 agentic decomposition-and-merging comparators using Tango, Tango 2, and TangoFlux. Table 5 additionally compares gated prompting against ordinary finetuning on both Tango and TangoFlux, substantially expanding the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: Equation 2 changes the reported relation-scoring aggregation from a product to a maximum. New TangoFlux experiments introduce frozen-backbone, single-prompt-type, and ungated controls. Existing dataset splits and original baseline inference settings are retained; the PDFs do not establish whether the scoring correction changed the implementation or caused retained results to be rerun.

E4.justification: v4 Section 6.4 and Table 6 add four targeted ablations testing backbone adaptation, relation prompts, event prompts, and gating. v1 contains no corresponding component study. Earlier qualitative examples and relation-specific radar analyses remain, including material moved to the appendix.

E5.justification: The seed information in Appendix Table I is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the compared results. The detector confidence thresholds are retained evaluation settings, not new uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The original benchmark values and Tango finetuning row are retained, while v4 adds TangoFlux, agentic, gated-prompt, and ablation results. Within v4 Table 5, gated prompting versus finetuning yields mAMSR values of 59.13 versus 48.67 for Tango and 127.98 versus 83.44 for TangoFlux, in the reported scaled units. Gains are not uniform: TangoFlux's gated variant scores lower on Count and Spatial Distance.

T1.justification: Equation 2 replaces the product of binary relation indicators with their maximum, aligning the mathematical expression with the retained statement that a satisfying subset is sufficient. This is a substantive but localized correction to the metric definition. The remaining scoring equations are retained, and no theoretical proofs are added.

C1.justification: The benchmark and relation-aware evaluation contributions remain. However, the abstract, contribution list, and conclusion replace ordinary finetuning as the principal intervention with gated prompt tuning, claiming improved relation modeling with approximately five million additional parameters. This substantially changes the paper's methodological contribution.

C2.justification: v4 introduces a domain-gap explanation for prompt-only adaptation failing, interprets the new agentic and component comparisons, and explicitly identifies the closed event/relation vocabulary as an applicability limitation. It removes v1's bag-of-words and unary-pretraining rationale and its explanation linking degraded Not performance to silent training targets. Earlier relation-difficulty interpretations are retained in Appendix F.

D1.justification: v4 supplies a substantially more concrete adaptation recipe: random 1024-dimensional prompts, specified trainable backbone components, Adam learning rate 3e-5, batch size 16, SNR gamma 5, 40 epochs, and four A100 GPUs. v1's Tango training description primarily names Adam and refers to the Tango 2 strategy. The PANNS recipe, original inference settings, and code link remain; TangoFlux inference settings are still absent from Table I.

R1.justification: v4 replaces the general audio-generation overview with positioning in NLP, visual, and acoustic prompt tuning, citing works such as Lester, Jia, Sohn, Liang, and Oiso. It adds TangoFlux and sparse-gating references while removing WavJourney and several references supporting v1's bag-of-words rationale. These changes substantially reposition the proposed intervention relative to prior research.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, related work, method, and experimental narrative are substantially revised. Data creation becomes a separate main section, while evaluation details, detailed benchmark findings, and the original extended conclusion move into appendices. A new short conclusion and explicit limitations section further reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: The document changes from a predominantly single-column to a two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figure 5 replaces the finetuning pipeline with the gated-prompt architecture; comparison tables gain new groupings and an ablation table is added. Earlier benchmark tables and radar plots remain, several relocated to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens evidence for the proposed intervention beyond v1's Tango finetuning demonstration: it compares adaptation on two backbones, evaluates agentic alternatives, and tests component necessity through four ablations. Concrete training settings and the Equation 2 correction also improve assessability. Benefits are tempered by nonuniform subgroup gains, removal of the relevant WavJourney discussion, and retained erroneous below-1% statements in Appendix Table IV, but the central methodological claims now have substantially stronger experimental support.
